s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Electrical pain radiating to the left hand
Weakness in fine movements and weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive neck pain
Pain radiates to the left hand
Numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
Weakness in fine movements of the left hand
Weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
Motor testing of the left hand revealed muscle strength of 3/5
Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra on CT
Lesion involves the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments
Lesion does not significantly compromise the thecal sac

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, intermediate to low signal on T1-weighted images, and heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar imaging features, such as osteolysis and soft tissue component, could suggest this diagnosis, although it was considered and excluded in the vignette

shortlist.label: Central giant cell lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multinucleated giant cells and osteolysis could suggest this diagnosis, although it was considered and excluded in the vignette

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location at the T1 vertebra and involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments could suggest this diagnosis, although it is less common than giant cell tumor of bone

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, as well as the patient's age, could suggest this diagnosis, although it is less likely than giant cell tumor of bone

raw.rationale: The presence of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, along with the involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments, is consistent with a giant cell tumor of bone. The patient's age and the description of the lesion on imaging studies, including heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Excluded due to distinct histologic features

rejected.label: Central giant cell lesion
rejected.why: Excluded due to specific distinguishing characteristics

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Not supported by the imaging characteristics and location of the lesion

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with different clinical and radiological features
